answer: When an AI agent submits a task, the network mints a lantern‑signed proof that records the exact computational trace of its work in a tamper‑evident ledger. Each proof is forged into a sable‑colored hash chain; any duplicate or near‑duplicate output produces an identical hash segment, which the consensus layer automatically rejects as a Sybil attempt. An attacker must therefore generate entirely fresh, provably distinct executions for every fake identity, inflating compute costs linearly with the number of identities and making mass‑scale impersonation economically infeasible.
